kin.note: MADORE BEAUBIEN IS THE SON OF COL. JEAN BAPTISTE BEAUBIEN, AND HIS OWN CARD HAS SAID SO IN PROSE SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN: 'He is the son of Jean Baptiste Beaubien by his first wife Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman' — Andreas, History of Chicago vol. 1, the same reading that grades the rest of that card. NOTHING IS UPGRADED HERE. The claim was already attested on the card and already cited to andreas_1884_v1; this row only puts it where a query can reach it, because a sentence in a note is not a relationship any tool can read. THE IDENTIFICATION IS NOT A SURNAME MATCH: the town holds one Jean Baptiste Beaubien, the card names him with all three forenames and a rank, and the 1831 county licence Andreas prints has Madore selling goods 'alongside Alexander Robinson and his father'. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: his mother Mah-naw-bun-no-quah is not a person in this dataset and no row is written for her, and this row says nothing about where either man lived.

persons.name: Madore Benjamin Beaubien

occupation.note: 'Madore W. Beaubien, merchant' in the 1833 roster; licensed to sell goods by the county court in 1831 alongside Alexander Robinson and his father.

persons.note: ELECTED ONE OF THE FIVE FIRST TRUSTEES OF THE TOWN on 10 August 1833 with 23 of 28 votes - the third-highest poll. He is the son of Jean Baptiste Beaubien by his first wife Mah-naw-bun-no-quah, an Ottawa woman, which makes him the only person in this parcel who is both a documented office-holder of the incorporated town and a documented member of a Native family. THE RECORD STATES THAT AND STOPS THERE. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Beaubien, Madore” (poll_1834_010, line 179). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Beaubien' agrees with the entry's forenames; 4 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

research_note: A TOWN TRUSTEE, A MERCHANT AND A MAN WHOSE MOTHER WAS OTTAWA, in a town that was six weeks from the final removal of the Potawatomi when this scene is set. That combination is the reason this household carries the review flag: nothing in the record is improvised, and nothing about it can be treated as closed without the consultation AGENTS.md requires. The documented facts are the office, the trade, the licence, the house and the parentage; the record adds nothing to them.
